searchedFor: reading BlockType and InlineStyle definitions in types.ts
finding.summary: import-export.md claims Docs Markdown export preserves "code", but the Docs model has no code/inline-code concept at all (no such Block or InlineStyle field), and serializeMarkdown has no handling for it.
finding.evidence: "headings, lists, links, bold/italic, code and tables survive" — but packages/docs/src/model/types.ts's BlockType is 'paragraph' | 'title' | 'subtitle' | 'heading' | 'list-item' | 'horizontal-rule' | 'table' | 'page-break' and InlineStyle has no code/monospace field; packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts has no code handling anywhere.

verdict.reason: The finding quotes import-export.md as claiming Markdown export preserves "code" ("headings, lists, links, bold/italic, code and tables survive"), but that sentence does not exist in the file. A grep for "code" in packages/documentation/guide/import-export.md returns no matches. The actual Markdown-export bullet (lines 50-56) lists what survives as "headings, lists, tables, links, images, bold, italic and strikethrough" and what does not as "alignment, indent, line spacing, colour, font choice and size, underline, super/subscript, merged and nested table cells, and headers/footers" — no mention of code/inline-code fidelity at all. Since the doc makes no claim about code blocks surviving export, there is no contradiction with the Docs model (BlockType/InlineStyle in packages/docs/src/model/types.ts, which indeed has no code concept) or with serializeMarkdown in packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts (which indeed has no code handling) — both facts the reviewer cited are accurate about the code, but irrelevant because the prose never asserts code round-trips.
